subject.title: core: el cron-handler devuelve 200 en fallos parciales y oculta degradaciones operativas

question: Should the first implementation phase keep HTTP 200 and add structured partial-failure status/severity, or should selected cron routes start returning 207/5xx immediately?
rationale: The source confirms the shared handler behavior, but changing response status affects many marketplace, general, data, and admin crons with different tolerance for partial batch failures.

options.title: Start with compatible structured signal
options.body: Add status, rejected counts, summarized reasons, and severity to responses/logs while keeping HTTP 200 until route-specific escalation is agreed.

options.title: Escalate selected routes now
options.body: Define the first route/fase severity matrix and change only those routes to 207/5xx with matching docs and validation.

options.title: Keep current 200 contract intentionally
options.body: Close the behavior as intentional only if maintainers decide that log-based partial-failure detection is sufficient for these cron surfaces.

recommendation.title: Start with compatible structured signal
recommendation.body: Add status, rejected counts, summarized reasons, and severity to responses/logs while keeping HTTP 200 until route-specific escalation is agreed.

likelyOwner.reason: The current handler implementation and recent cron/marketplace documentation history point to JavierHamelyn as the best available owner for the severity-contract decision.
